Innovation should remember the person.

My thoughts on user experience and the commercial purpose of innovation.

2 minute readPersonal portfolio · 2026A personal perspective

My thoughts on user experience and the commercial purpose of innovation.

  • My post about CEER’s EXOBOT models focused on innovation designed around practical needs. I was interested in the relationship between advanced technology and the experience of the person using a product. The commercial question was not simply how much technology could be added, but which decisions made it useful.
  • I wrote about cabin comfort in Saudi Arabia's climate and the value of keeping physical controls for essential functions. Those details caught my attention because they brought the conversation back to an ordinary person using the product. A small design choice can matter more when it affects something someone does repeatedly.
  • A useful next question is how a company understands the needs of its intended audience. Which features answer an actual problem? What trade-offs are being made? What information would help a reader judge whether the proposed benefit has been demonstrated?
  • My current interest in corporate law includes understanding businesses as organisations making decisions. A product announcement offers one small window into that work: an ambition, an intended customer, a practical setting, and assumptions about what will create value.
01 / 04

A detail that changed the emphasis

My post about CEER’s EXOBOT models focused on innovation designed around practical needs.

I was interested in the relationship between advanced technology and the experience of the person using a product. The commercial question was not simply how much technology could be added, but which decisions made it useful.

The connection

That perspective connects to the events I have attended.

Read the deeper context+

A demonstration can make a new capability visible. Understanding a product requires asking what problem it is meant to solve and how the design fits the conditions in which someone will use it.

02 / 04

Keeping the user in the picture

I wrote about cabin comfort in Saudi Arabia's climate and the value of keeping physical controls for essential functions.

Those details caught my attention because they brought the conversation back to an ordinary person using the product. A small design choice can matter more when it affects something someone does repeatedly.

The connection

I was responding to a product announcement, so what interested me was the reasoning behind the design.

Read the deeper context+

Which needs had the company chosen to focus on? How would the controls or cabin features fit an everyday experience? Those questions gave me more to think about than a list of performance figures.

03 / 04

A commercial perspective worth developing

A useful next question is how a company understands the needs of its intended audience.

Which features answer an actual problem? What trade-offs are being made? What information would help a reader judge whether the proposed benefit has been demonstrated?

The connection

My sales, administration, and finance courses help me approach the commercial side of those questions.

Read the deeper context+

I want to understand the promised value, the intended user, and the organisation behind the product. Reading an announcement with those different angles in mind makes it easier to see what I understand and what I would want to know next.

04 / 04

The connection to my direction

My current interest in corporate law includes understanding businesses as organisations making decisions.

A product announcement offers one small window into that work: an ambition, an intended customer, a practical setting, and assumptions about what will create value.

The connection

The thought I want to carry forward is to keep the person using a product in view.

Read the deeper context+

Innovation becomes more interesting when I understand its purpose, and design becomes more useful when it responds to that purpose. I want to bring that question into more of my commercial reading, not only automotive announcements.

Where this reflection began

This essay grew from the original post linked below. I have expanded the thought here as part of my own learning and writing.
